title: Right triangles & trigonometry: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Right triangles & trigonometry: Visual Guide

1. Ratios Not Lengths | two leg sliders plus a scale slider on one right triangle, with sin, cos and tan written out as SOH-CAH-TOA equations over the live side lengths | scaling a triangle changes every length and no ratio, which is why sine, cosine and tangent are functions of the angle alone and can live on a calculator key

2. Pick The Ratio | six know/want side pairs, an angle slider and a known-length slider, with all three ratios answering and only one being right | the pair of sides you name selects the ratio uniquely, and the wrong ratio returns a clean plausible number with no warning — except at 45 degrees, where sin and cos collide and hide the mistake entirely

3. Inverse Undoes It | two leg sliders and a switch over which pair of sides you were given, showing the inverse key beside the forward key pressed by mistake | two sides known means an inverse trigonometric function; all three pairs recover the same angle, and applying the forward function to a ratio returns a tiny decimal that is a ratio, not an angle

4. Flip Or Complement | the same triangle under two modes, complementary angles and reciprocal ratios, with both acute angles arced and the shared side marked | sin θ = cos(90−θ) because one physical side is opposite one acute angle and adjacent to the other, while csc, sec and cot are only that fraction upside down — and at 45 degrees both relationships degenerate into coincidences that teach the wrong rule

5. Ladder Ramp Elevation | three word-problem scenarios (ladder on a wall, ramp rise and run, angle of elevation) each with two draggable givens and a sketch-label-ratio-solve worked block | modelling is four moves in order, and the ratio falls out of the sketch: hypotenuse plus angle means sine and cosine, two legs mean tangent and Pythagoras, horizontal distance plus elevation means tangent
